# Third-party code

| Directory | Project | License | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| `libmspub/` | [libmspub](https://wiki.documentfoundation.org/DLP/Libraries/libmspub), the `.pub` file parser | MPL-2.0 | see `libmspub/VERSION` |
| `librevenge/` | [librevenge](https://sourceforge.net/p/libwpd/librevenge/), document interfaces and OLE2 streams | MPL-2.0 or LGPL-2.1+ | 0.0.5 |
| `compat/` | JeffPub's minimal stand-ins for the Boost headers these libraries use | GPL-3.0 (this project) | — |
| `ffmpeg/licenses/` | The notice and license text of the [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/) libraries that come with JeffDeck (for its movies and sounds, through Qt Multimedia), shipped with JeffDeck's packages. `ffmpeg-components.txt` lists what is compiled into them | LGPL-2.1+ | 7.1.5 (built here, `tools/build_ffmpeg.sh`) |
| `qpdf/licenses/` | The license text of [qpdf](https://qpdf.org/) (Apache-2.0; it is also offered under the Artistic License 2.0) and its notice, shipped with every package. qpdf 12.4.2 is built from its release tarball (`cmake/qpdf.cmake`, checked against its SHA-256), as a static library with its own crypto code, to write PDFs with a password | Apache-2.0 | 12.4.2 |
| `libjpeg_turbo/licenses/` | The license texts of [libjpeg-turbo](https://libjpeg-turbo.org/), which qpdf reads JPEG streams with; built from its release tarball without SIMD (`cmake/qpdf.cmake`) | IJG and BSD-3-Clause | 3.2.1 |
| `qpdfwrap/` | The one file that includes qpdf's C++20 headers, behind an interface of standard types | GPL-3.0 (this project) | — |
| `pdfium/licenses/` | The license texts of [PDFium](https://pdfium.googlesource.com/pdfium/) and of the libraries built into it, shipped with every package | see below | chromium/8086 (157.0.8086.0) |

zlib is downloaded at build time when the system has none. qpdf and libjpeg-turbo are downloaded when the build directory is made, and checked against their SHA-256; `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_QPDF` and `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_LIBJPEG_TURBO` name unpacked copies for a build that must not download.

## FFmpeg

JeffDeck links Qt Multimedia, whose FFmpeg backend decodes the movies and sounds it plays. Qt ships a full FFmpeg (7.1.5: about 350 file readers, 500 decoders, and 180 writers, and every one is a way in for a file from a stranger), so JeffOffice builds its own from the official source release instead: `tools/build_ffmpeg.sh` downloads `ffmpeg-7.1.5.tar.xz` from ffmpeg.org, checks its SHA-256 (pinned in the script) before unpacking, and builds shared libraries with the same major versions as Qt's (libavcodec 61, libavformat 61, libavutil 59, libswresample 5, libswscale 8), so Qt's plugin loads them unchanged. The build is LGPL 2.1 or later only (a GPL, version 3, or nonfree option fails the script), with no network, no programs, no devices, no hardware decoders, no encoders, no muxers, no filters library, and no other libraries but zlib (`--disable-everything --disable-autodetect`; zlib opens a movie's compressed header and compressed Matroska tracks: the system's on Linux and macOS, MSYS2's static copy on Windows).

What a presentation holds decides what is kept (the evidence is below). Only these are compiled in:

- Readers: mov (MP4, M4A, 3GP, QuickTime), matroska (MKV, WebM), avi, asf (WMV, WMA), mpegps, mpegts, mpegvideo, wav, mp3, aac, flac, ogg, aiff.
- Video: h264, hevc, mpeg4, h263, mpeg1video, mpeg2video, msmpeg4v1/v2/v3, wmv1/2/3, vc1, vp8, vp9, mjpeg, cinepak, msvideo1, rawvideo.
- Audio: aac, ac3, eac3, mp2, mp3, wmav1/2, wmapro, wmalossless, flac, vorbis, opus, alac, the PCM variants (8, 16, 24, and 32 bit; float; A-law and mu-law), adpcm_ms, adpcm_ima_wav, adpcm_ima_qt.
- Their parsers, and the file protocol alone (JeffDeck hands the player its bytes from memory and restricts protocols besides).

On a Mac the build also has VideoToolbox's device type (not its hardware decoders or encoders: Qt's plugin for a Mac imports one of its helper functions, and without it the plugin does not load), and its libraries re-export the ones they use, as Qt's do (`tools/check_macho_binds.py` checks every import of the plugin). `ffmpeg-components.txt` is the list of what a build compiled in, written by the script; `tools/check_ffmpeg_components.py` (run by CI) fails if the script or that file has a banned component or a flag it must not have (the VobSub, RTP, RTSP, and SDP readers, the NVDEC accelerator, the S/PDIF writer, and the ADX decoder among them: they are the parts of the full build named in the 2026 flaws CVE-2026-64830, -64832, -64833, -64834, and -64835), or the two differ. The snap builds the FFmpeg its Qt binds to, read from the NEEDED entries of the KDE SDK's `libffmpegmediaplugin.so` (`tools/ffmpeg_for_plugin.sh`): 7.1.5 for libavcodec 61, as above (the content snap's Qt 6.11), or 6.1.6 for libavcodec 60 (`FFMPEG_VERSION=6.1.6`, `ffmpeg-components-6.1.6.txt`); any other set stops the build. The build also checks that the libraries export every function that plugin imports (`FFMPEG_PLUGIN`). They replace the distribution's, which the Ubuntu archive carries without the fixes for the 2026 flaws, and the content snap's full copy: they sit in `usr/lib/jeffoffice-ffmpeg`, which every app puts first in its `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, and `tools/snap_ffmpeg_audit.py` (the snap workflow) resolves the plugin's libraries in the built snap the way the apps do and fails unless every one is ours. `tools/use_ffmpeg.sh` puts the build in a CI runner's own copy of Qt, so the tests run on it and the deployment tools copy it into the packages, and checks that the packages hold it. They are not changed beyond their configuration.

Evidence for the list: the public test collections (`tests/` does not carry them) hold 103 `.pptx` and `.odp` decks and 1,083 `.ppt` decks; the media in them are 1 MP4 (H.264 and AAC), 1 MP3, and, in the `.ppt` decks, 71 with WAV sounds, almost all PCM and some ADPCM of the Windows kind. The rest of the list is the formats JeffDeck's Insert Video and Insert Audio dialogs offer (`apps/deck/core/media.cpp`, `kFiles`) and those their codecs need, and the older AVI and Windows Media codecs a long-lived deck may hold. Left out: Ogg Theora, FLV (Flash video), AV1 (FFmpeg's own decoder needs a graphics card, and the software decoders are separate libraries), DTS, TrueHD, and AMR audio, subtitles, and MIDI (FFmpeg never played it).

What happens to a file in a format that is left out, found by playing the samples in `tests/data/media` (`tests/deck/tst_deck_media.cpp`): a movie in a format the build has no reader or decoder for is not played, and the player says "This movie can't be played" (Insert refuses a file it can't read at all, with a message that names the file; one whose container it reads but whose picture it can't decode goes on the slide as a dark frame, and the message comes when it is played); a movie whose picture is kept but whose sound is in a format left out is refused the same way, as a whole, not played as a picture without sound: the FFmpeg backend opens every stream of the file, a sound included, whether or not the computer has an audio output (found with the sample in `tests/data/media/audio_dropped` on a machine with no audio output, as on CI).  Qt's default backend is FFmpeg on Windows, macOS, and Linux (6.8 and 6.11), but Qt 6.11, unlike 6.8, goes on to another backend (the system's own on Windows and macOS, which reads other formats) when the FFmpeg plugin can't be loaded, so a test (`theFFmpegBackendIsTheOneThatPlays`) fails when the backend that plays is not FFmpeg. Nothing hangs. The Insert dialogs do not offer Ogg video or MIDI files.

Where the flaws are: NVD describes CVE-2026-64834 as an infinite loop in the RTP/ASF demuxer, `libavformat/rtpdec_asf.c` (the function `rtp_asf_fix_header`, reached by an RTP stream), not the ASF file demuxer; `rtpdec_asf` is compiled only with the RTP demuxer, which this build leaves out, so the ASF file reader (`asf`, for WMV and WMA files) stays; its object file is not in the build and the library has no `rtp_asf` symbol. (The NVD record: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-64834, checked on Nov 9, 2026.) The other four are in components this build does not have (the VobSub demuxer, NVDEC, the S/PDIF muxer, the ADX decoder). `tools/ffmpeg_probe.c` loads the built libraries and lists what is inside them, on every system the build runs on (and the snap's): CI compares that with what the script allows and with the list a good build reports (`third_party/ffmpeg-runtime-7.1.5.txt`, `-6.1.6.txt`), so a component added by any means shows up.

Where the source comes from: the release tarballs (`ffmpeg-7.1.5.tar.xz` and `ffmpeg-6.1.6.tar.xz`) are fetched only from https://ffmpeg.org/releases/. Their SHA-256 values in `tools/build_ffmpeg.sh` were checked on Nov 9, 2026 against the detached signatures (`.asc`) that ffmpeg.org publishes beside them: both are good signatures by the FFmpeg release signing key, fingerprint `FCF9 86EA 15E6 E293 A564 4F10 B432 2F04 D676 58D8` (the key file is https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-devel.asc; its fingerprint is the one the project lists). The script checks the SHA-256 and deletes a download that fails it.

## PDFium

PDFium places PDF pages as pictures (`libs/base/render/pdfpage.cpp`). The build downloads the prebuilt library from [bblanchon/pdfium-binaries](https://github.com/bblanchon/pdfium-binaries) release `chromium/8086` and checks it against its SHA-256 (`cmake/pdfium.cmake`); it isn't modified. The texts in `pdfium/licenses/` come from that release (`LICENSE`, saved as `pdfium-binaries.txt`, and `licenses/`); update them with the version.

## JeffPub changes

These are the only modifications to the upstream sources. Each is marked with a `JeffPub` comment.

- **Latin font slot.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` (`getFontIndex`) reads a run's font from slot 0 of its font container (0x24), the slot for Latin text; a run with fonts for other scripts only takes its font from its style. Upstream took the first slot, so text in older newsletters whose runs list Courier New and Sendnya for other scripts came in as Courier New where Publisher shows Gill Sans MT. Publisher 2000 and 98 files hold each slot's font number directly instead of in a container per slot; upstream skipped those, so their runs all came in as the first font in the table (Times New Roman where Publisher shows Arial or Arial Rounded MT Bold).
- **Linked box order.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads each text box's place in its story's chain (shape block 0x28; the first box has none) and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it on as `jp:text-chain-index`. Upstream links boxes in the order the file draws them, so a story could start in its second or third box (columns of a newsletter in the wrong order).
- **Long text.** `MSPUBParser.h` keeps the text stream positions of character and paragraph runs as 32-bit numbers. Upstream stores them in 16 bits, which wrap past 64 KB of text, so in any publication with more than about 32,000 characters every story after that point opened empty (a four-page newsletter lost pages 2 to 4). Found by comparing every page with Publisher's own rendering.
- **No Boost.** `compat/boost/*` provides `optional` (on `std::optional`), `cstdint`, `numeric_cast`, a 2-D `multi_array`, and `trim`. librevenge's Boost.Spirit number parsing (`RVNGPropertyList.cpp`) and Boost.Archive base64 (`RVNGBinaryData.cpp`) are rewritten in plain C++.
- **No ICU.** libmspub decodes UTF-16LE and windows-1252 itself. Other legacy codepages go through `libmspub::setDecodeHook()` (`inc/libmspub/jp_hooks.h`), which JeffPub implements with Qt. A small LCID table replaces `uloc_getLocaleForLCID`, and the encoding guess for Publisher 97/98 files defaults to windows-1252.
- **Linked text boxes.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` adds a `jp:text-id` property to each text object, so text boxes that share one story can be linked again on import. Upstream emits the full story into every box.
- **Text direction.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the OfficeArt `txflTextFlow` property (0x0088) and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it on as `jp:text-flow`, so rotated text such as book spines imports as vertical text. Upstream ignores it and the text stacks letter by letter.
- **Normal style inheritance.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` gives paragraphs that name no style the document's Normal style (style sheet entry 0), which carries the default line spacing (typically 1.19 sp) and space after. It also reports the spacing in sp as `jp:line-spacing-sp`, including an explicit 1 sp. Upstream falls back to a flat 1 sp.
- **Text outline.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the character "line" container (0x59): outline color index and width. `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them as `jp:text-outline-color` and `jp:text-outline-width`.
- **Table cell fills and borders.** Publisher stores each formatted cell's fill, and each ruled line, as a drawing shape with no page placement whose client anchor names the table (see `TableCellFormat` in `TableInfo.h`). `MSPUBParser.cpp` collects them and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` emits them as `fo:background-color` and `fo:border-*` on the cells. Upstream ignores them, so formatted tables import blank. Worked out from four one-change sample files (fill, horizontal and vertical borders).
- **Table cell settings.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads each table cell's Text Direction (field 06: 2 turns its text a quarter turn), vertical alignment (07: 1 middle, 2 bottom), division by a diagonal (05), and margins (0a-0d), the first three from their low bytes only (Publisher's files have stray bits above it in 05 and 07); `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them on as `jp:text-direction`, `style:vertical-align`, `jp:diagonal`, and `fo:padding-*`. Upstream reads only the cell's place.
- **Divided table cells.** A cell divided by a diagonal is two records at one place: the first half in the cell's place in the list, the second listed after the grid's cells. `createTableLayout` in `MSPUBCollector.cpp` pairs them, the cell's text is its first half's followed by the second's with the second half's first paragraph marked `jp:second-half`, and the diagonal's own line (a table formatting shape of kind 3, `TableInfo.h`, whose color is the shape's line color) goes on as `jp:diagonal-border`. Upstream made the second record the cell, so the first half and its text were lost.
- **Damaged tables.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` leaves out a table of more than 256 rows or 256 columns (twice Publisher's largest), one whose row or column count doesn't match its edges, one whose cell list isn't in the file, and one that lacks a count, and goes on with the rest of the file. Upstream made every cell of any size (a file of a few KB could ask for gigabytes) and failed the whole file for the other three.
- **Arrowheads.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes each line's start and end arrowheads (style 1-5 as stored, and size) on as `jp:arrow-start`, `jp:arrow-end`, and their `-size` properties. Upstream reads them but never emits them, so arrows import as plain lines.
- **Text Art.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads Text Art's words (0x00C0), font (0x00C5), alignment, size, spacing, and settings (0x00C2-0x00C4, 0x00FF), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` hands them on as `jp:textart-*` with the shape type, unturned frame, rotation, and flips (through `drawRectangle`) instead of drawing the warp's guide curves. Upstream drops Text Art.
- **Text-valued properties.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads Text Art words and font, and picture and shape names, as plain bytes of their stated length. Upstream reads every long property as a list, which misreads text and loses the properties that follow it.
- **Master pages and special pages.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` writes each master page's objects once, inside `startMasterPage`/`endMasterPage`, before the pages, and names each page's master as `jp:master-seq`; upstream paints master objects onto every page. Every real page is written, including pages with no objects of their own (upstream drops them). Special pages (envelope, web, and the like: up to four entries at the end of the document's page list, recognized by sequence number, a page kind of 0 in the first byte of field 06, or being blank) are left out; upstream recognizes them only by four fixed sequence numbers, which older files don't use.
- **Tabs, lists, strikethrough, letter spacing.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads each tab stop's alignment, the list kind and bullet character from their own sub-blocks (upstream read the container's value, so lists never came through), the numbering punctuation (0x58), strikethrough (0x10), added letter spacing (0x1B), and tracking (0x1F). `MSPUBCollector.cpp` emits tab stops as `style:tab-stops`, lists as `jp:list-kind`, `jp:list-char`, `jp:list-delim`, and the rest as `style:text-line-through-type`, `fo:letter-spacing`, and `jp:tracking`.
- **Line transparency.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a line's opacity (0x01C1) and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it on as `svg:stroke-opacity`. Upstream ignores it, so see-through lines import solid.
- **Picture settings.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads grayscale and black and white (0x013F) and the color shown clear (0x0107); `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them on as `jp:picture-gray`, `jp:picture-bilevel`, and `jp:transparent-color`, with the stored brightness and contrast as `jp:brightness` and `jp:contrast`. Upstream reads contrast but drops it, and ignores the rest.
- **Picture crops and see-through pictures.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a picture's crops (0x0100-0x0103) and a picture fill's opacity (0x0182), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them on as `jp:crop-*` and `jp:picture-opacity`, page backgrounds included. Upstream ignores both, so cropped pictures came in squeezed into their frames and see-through pictures solid.
- **Shape identity.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes every shape's number with its unturned frame, rotation, and flips (`jp:shape-type`, `jp:frame-*`), so the importer can bring a preset back as that preset instead of a freeform outline, and can tell which outline belongs to which fill.
- **Lists from paragraph styles.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` takes a paragraph's list (bullet or numbering, its character, size, font, and punctuation) from its named paragraph style when the paragraph has none of its own, as indents already were. Upstream read only the paragraph's own list, so the bulleted lists of Publisher's newsletter and flyer designs, whose bullets live in a style, came in without bullets.
- **Gradient angles and turning.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` and `Fill.cpp` pass a gradient's stored angle (0x018B, signed 16.16) on whole as `jp:fill-angle`, and `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the tertiary fill flags (0x01BF), where 0x20 with its use bit 0x200000 makes the fill turn and flip with its shape; `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes that on as `jp:fill-turns`. Publisher runs the first color toward 270 - *a* for a stored angle *a* of 0 or more and toward 90 - *a* for a negative one. Upstream's `draw:angle` is right only for the negative angles of Publisher's built-in designs, so angles set in Publisher's Fill Effects dialog (0-359) came in mirrored, and it doesn't report turning.
- **Freeforms built from formulas.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a freeform's formulas (pGuides, 0xC156: 8-byte entries of a code and three signed arguments), which upstream left a FIXME, and its whole coordinate space (0x0140-0x0143, often -32000 to 32000; upstream assumed it starts at 0). `PolygonUtils.cpp` takes only 0x8000nnnn as a formula reference (upstream took any value with the top bit set, so -32000 became a formula), `MSPUBCollector.cpp` evaluates operation 6 as "if greater than 0" (upstream: "if not 0"), and an adjust value used as a sine or cosine angle is read in 16.16 degrees. Upstream drew Publisher's formula freeforms (curved page edges, corner circles, bracket boxes) as empty three-point paths; in 3,982 of Publisher's designs only the 261 with such shapes change. `MSPUBCollector.cpp` works each formula out once per point (a formula can refer to an earlier one up to three times, so a crafted chain took exponential time) and treats a result that isn't a finite number as 0; the coordinate space's width is computed in 64 bits.
- **A picture's own fill.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` keeps a picture shape's solid fill (0x0181 with the filled flag) as `jp:picture-back-color` before the picture takes the fill's place. Publisher paints it behind the picture, so it shows through a metafile's clear parts (a pinwheel's teal and yellow blades); upstream dropped it.
- **Shadow colors from the shape's colors.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` starts a shadow color given as a change of the shape's own color (flag 0x10 with index 0xF0, its fill, or 0xF2, its line; Publisher's default text box shadow is its line color lightened halfway) from that color. Upstream changed the reference's own bytes, so a gray shadow came out pink.
- **Line corners.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a line's corner style (lineJoinStyle, 0x01D6: 0 bevel, 1 miter, 2 round) and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it on as `jp:line-join`. Publisher's designs store 2 for many shapes; without it Publisher draws mitered corners. Upstream ignores it.
- **Outlines on the frame.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` draws a rectangle's outline on the shape's own frame. Upstream pushed each edge out by half of that side's line, taking one line per side, so a plain outline (one line) moved only its top edge: a sign's 12-point frame drawn inside its edge sat 6 points too high.
- **Outlines inside the edge.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the inset-pen flag (0x40, with its use bit) of a shape's line properties (0x01FF) in either property table, and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it on as `jp:line-inset`. Publisher draws such outlines inside the shape's edge (text box borders, picture frames, and many design frames); upstream ignores the flag.
- **Octagon proportions.** `PolygonUtils.cpp` gives an octagon with no proportion of its own Publisher's default, 6326 (corners cut at 29.3% of each side: a regular octagon). Upstream's 5000 cut them at 23.1%, so a stop sign's octagon came out squatter than Publisher draws it.
- **Superscript and subscript.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the character property 0x0F from its low byte. Publisher keeps flags in the high byte (0xF001, 0xB601, and others mean superscript), and upstream took any value above 2 as neither, so ordinals like "5th" lost their raised letters.
- **Default text color.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` marks a run without a color of its own (its color comes from the default style, or is the fallback black) with `jp:color-default`, so a link without a color of its own shows in the link color as in Publisher, not black.
- **Hyphenation.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the story list (Contents chunk 0x65), where a story's record carries a `04` flag when its text isn't hyphenated automatically, and its `0a` hyphenation zone in EMUs (left out at the default of 0.25 inch), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` marks those text boxes `jp:no-hyphenation` and `jp:hyphenation-zone`, and a table the same way, since all of a table's cells are one story. Upstream skips the chunk. Matched against the PDFs of the .pub files on hand, every file whose line breaks changed agreed with the flag.
- **Default tab stop.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the text stream's SGP section, whose one property `00:22` is the publication's default tab stop in EMU (Publisher's default tab stop; the section is empty at 36 points), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` hands it to `startDocument` as `jp:default-tab-stop` in inches. Upstream skips the section. Worked out from files Publisher saved with 14.4, 20, 72, and 100 points.
- **AutoFit Text.** The same story records carry the AutoFit Text setting: `05` (low bits 1 = Best Fit, 3 = Shrink Text On Overflow; `08` then holds the font size before shrinking) and a `0c` flag for Grow Text Box to Fit. `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads them and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` marks the text box `jp:autofit` (1 best fit, 2 shrink, 3 grow). Found by choosing each setting in Publisher and saving; across 655 text boxes in 284 publications it agrees with the setting Publisher reports for all but 8, which the check couldn't match to a single box.
- **Layout type.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the DOCUMENT chunk's field 0x11 (1 booklet, 3 folded card, 7 envelope) and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it on each page as `jp:layout`. Upstream skips it.
- **Publisher 2000 scratch area.** `MSPUBParser2k.cpp` treats a page chunk without a canvas size (bytes 12-19 zero) as the scratch area, not a page; upstream made it a page wherever objects sat on it, so 2000 and 98 files opened with an extra page (the public 2000 and 98 samples with 3 pages where Publisher shows 2).
- **Booklet pages and two-page masters.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` keeps the pages of a booklet or folded card that Publisher marks 0 in field 06 (all but the first; elsewhere a 0 there marks a special page), and `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads each master's side (field 10: 1 right-hand, 0 left-hand part, 3 single) and name, which the collector passes on as `jp:master-side` and `jp:master-name` so the two parts make one two-page master. Upstream opens such a booklet with one page.
- **Objects in text.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads each story's EOBJ section (its objects' character positions and numbers) and a shape's number (shape field 0f), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` writes those shapes once, with the first page, marked `jp:inline-num` (left off their own page, which Publisher never shows), and gives each U+FFFC its story lists a span of its own with the same mark. Upstream drops the objects and leaves the U+FFFC.
- **Fields and hyperlinks.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads character properties `00` (type 0x12) and `22` (type 0x22) into the character style, and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` marks a page number's "#" (`00` low byte 5) with `jp:field` = `page`, `page:next`, or `page:prev` (`22` = -1, -7, -6). The parser also reads each story's TOKN section (dates, times, and hyperlinks, with their formats and addresses), and the collector cuts runs where one starts or ends: a date's first piece gets `jp:field` = `pubdate:<format>` (any later ones `jp:field-cont`), a hyperlink's pieces sit inside `openLink`. Upstream shows the "#" and keeps dates as fixed text and hyperlinks as plain text.
- **Text wrapping.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the shape chunk's field 04 (its low byte: 0 none, 2 tight, 3 through, 4 top and bottom; left out for square) and the drawing's wrap distances (0x0384-0x0387), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them on as `jp:wrap` and `jp:wrap-left`/`-top`/`-right`/`-bottom`. Upstream reads neither.
- **Connectors.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads each drawing's connector rules (solver container 0xF005, one 0xF012 rule per connector: shape A, shape B, the connector, and the connection site on A and B, by drawing shape id) and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` marks the connector `jp:glue-start-seq`/`-site` and `jp:glue-end-seq`/`-site`, with `jp:shape-seq` on every shape so the attachments can be matched to the objects. A line or connector whose color is Publisher's default (black) records no color; upstream drew no line for it. Checked against connectors attached through Publisher.
- **Style names.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the first style sheet (STSH 0), keeping every entry inside its section and losing only names when it is damaged, where each style has a name (Publisher's built-in styles have none and a negative id; -1 is Normal), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes a paragraph's named style on as `jp:style-name`, with the style's own bold and italic as `jp:style-bold` and `jp:style-italic` (bold and italic in a run switch the style's on or off).
- **Bullet size and font.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a list paragraph's bullet or number size (paragraph property 0x02) and the bullet's font (0x03, an index into the font table), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them on as `jp:list-size` in points and `jp:list-font` by name. With `JP_PUB_TRACE` set, the parser also prints the font table.
- **List indent.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a list paragraph's indent (property 0x06: where its text starts from the text area's edge, or at the bullet's end; 0 on a right-to-left paragraph) and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it on as `jp:list-indent` in points, taking the paragraph style's when the paragraph has none. Upstream ignores it.
- **A font named "inherit".** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` takes a run in a font named `inherit` (the CSS word, left in the font table by text pasted from a web page) as having no font, so it reads in its style's, as Publisher draws it.
- **Process colors.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` decodes a fill's process inks from the tertiary properties 0x019F and 0x01A6 (with 0x019E, the color as shown), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them on as whole numbers 0-255 (`jp:ink-c`, `jp:ink-m`, `jp:ink-y`, `jp:ink-k`; never as formatted text, which follows the system's decimal separator) when the fill is that color.
- **Line spacing in points without a flag ("At least").** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a paragraph's line spacing (0x34) with neither low bit set as points, in eighths of an EMU like the flagged kind (1219200 is 12 pt), but as a minimum: Publisher's "At least", where the points kind with its flag set is "Exactly". `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it on as `jp:line-height-min` ("Exactly" stays `fo:line-height`). Upstream dropped it, so the paragraph took its style's spacing: a booklet's list that Publisher double-spaces came in at 1.19 lines.
- **Letter spacing from styles.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` gives a run that sets neither letter spacing (0x1B) nor tracking (0x1F) its paragraph style's, and `MSPUBParser.cpp` marks a run that sets 0x1B itself (its own 0 stays). Upstream used only the run's own, so a sign whose headline style tightens its letters (87.5% and 3 points) came in 8% wider than Publisher draws it.
- **Underline kinds.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` adds ODF's `style:text-underline-mode` = `skip-white-space` for an underline under words only, and marks a thick long dash bold like the other thick kinds. Upstream sends words only as a plain underline.
- **Locale-proof numbers.** `libmspub_utils.cpp` adds `fixedNumber()`, which writes numbers with a '.' whatever the system's language; it replaces the `%f` formatting of table rule widths (`MSPUBCollector.cpp`) and clip paths (`PolygonUtils.cpp`), which on a German or French system wrote a ',' and turned a 1.5 pt rule into a hairline.
- **Default white fill.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` fills a shape that is marked filled but names no fill color with white, the drawing format's default. Upstream leaves such shapes unfilled, so they vanish (the white stars in a party invitation template).
- **Spot colors.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a fill's spot ink name (complex property 0x01A1 in the extra-properties record, `P2,#<color>,<ink name>`) and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it with the fill's inks as `jp:ink-spot`.
- **Tracing.** With `JP_PUB_TRACE` set, the parser prints style sheets, unknown character properties, shape records, drawing properties (including complex values), the content chunk list (with its free slots), table and cell records, every shape visited and painted, and the text-stream chunk list. This is used to reverse-engineer fields that are still unread.
- Unused librevenge generators and the directory stream are not built.
- **Metadata is optional.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` ignores errors while reading document properties instead of failing the whole import (affects two sample files in Apache POI's test set).
- **Damaged OLE headers.** `RVNGOLEStream.cpp` rejects impossible block sizes instead of asserting (found by Apache POI's fuzz files).
